label: Mixed Light Balance
blurb: Evens out a shot lit by two colours of light at once: a warm lamp on one side and blue daylight from a window on the other, an orange street light against a white phone torch, a room half lit by a monitor. A normal white balance can only fix one of them. This measures the colour of the light area by area from the surfaces that should be neutral, ignoring strongly coloured things, and balances each area on its own in real light with brightness kept, either towards the shot's overall light so the mood stays or all the way to neutral white.
